habitat: Flocks in a variety of woodland, especially on Kalahari sands. It hawks from a perch, often near pans and dry riverbeds. Nomadic when not breeding.
summary: A common resident, nomadic when not breeding. Green above and on the upper breast, a yellow throat with a blue band, and a blue belly and forked tail. The immature lacks the yellow and blue throat and is pale apple-green below; the colour key says the immature is apple-green above and below. The call is a soft kwit kwit. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident and also says it is nomadic when not breeding. Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged. Population figures were left unchanged.

similar.note: Little Bee-eater has a square tail, orange-buff to rufous underparts and a black breast-band. Swallow-tailed Bee-eater has a bright blue collar, bluish underparts and a forked blue tail.
